Let the wall temperature excess be

\[
\theta_s(x)=T_s(x)-T_\infty=\frac{A}{x},
\]

with \(A>0\) for heating and \(A<0\) for cooling. The local Rayleigh number is

\[
Ra_x=\frac{g\beta \theta_s(x) x\,Pr}{\nu^2}
      =\frac{g\beta A\,Pr}{\nu^2},
\]

so \(Ra_x\) is independent of \(x\). For laminar natural convection this is the key self-similarity condition: the local Nusselt number is constant,

\[
Nu_x = \frac{q''x}{k\theta_s(x)} = \text{constant}.
\]

Hence the power-law variations with \(x\) are:

| Variable | Variation with \(x\) |
|---|---|
| Local heat flux \(q''(x)\) | \(q''(x)\propto x^{-2}\) |
| Total heat rate \(Q(x)\) | \(Q(x)\propto x^{-1}\), more exactly \(Q(x)=C\left(\frac{1}{x_0}-\frac{1}{x}\right)\) for a finite starting point \(x_0\) |
| Boundary-layer thickness \(\delta(x)\) | \(\delta(x)\propto x\) |
| Maximum velocity \(u_{\max}(x)\) | \(u_{\max}(x)\propto x^{-1}\) |
| External normal velocity \(v(\infty)\) | velocity scale \(\propto x^{-1}\); in the exact constant- \(Ra_x\) self-similar solution the integrated far-field normal velocity is zero because the tangential flow rate is constant |

A compact form is:

\[
q'' \sim \frac{kA\,Nu_0}{x^2},
\qquad
Q \sim kA\,Nu_0\left(\frac{1}{x_0}-\frac{1}{x}\right),
\]

\[
\delta \sim \frac{x}{Nu_0},
\qquad
u_{\max} \sim \frac{(g\beta A\nu)^{1/2}}{x},
\]

and the normal-velocity scale is

\[
v(\infty) \sim \frac{u_{\max}\delta}{x} \sim \frac{(g\beta A\nu)^{1/2}}{x}.
\]

In the exact self-similar constant-Rayleigh solution, the tangential flow rate through the boundary layer is constant, so the far-field normal velocity \(v(\infty)\) tends to zero; the \(x^{-1}\) scaling is the local normal-velocity scale within or at the edge of the boundary layer.

**Physical obtainability:**  
Yes, this flow can be physically realized if the surface starts at a finite distance \(x_0>0\) from the singular point \(x=0\), so that the wall temperature and heat flux remain finite. It would arise when the wall temperature is imposed as

\[
T_s(x)=T_\infty+\frac{A}{x},
\]

or when a distributed heat source produces a local heat flux \(q''(x)\propto x^{-2}\), giving a cumulative heat rate that varies as \(1/x\). This is a steady, laminar, buoyancy-driven boundary layer with constant local Rayleigh number, no imposed crossflow, constant ambient temperature, and constant fluid properties.
